label: End-of-episode (low value) a2-committed: rewarded D1 or rare S1 after a2
explanation: Fires only in the last ~10 trials of an episode (99.7% of mass at ep_trial 90-99; never before trial 80), which shows up as the model value output dropping below ~5 (100% of mass in the lowest value bin). Within that window it is specific to a2: 99.5% of mass on trials where the agent chooses a2. It is active at D1 (74% of mass, mostly when the previous reward was 1) and at D2 when a2 led rarely to S1 (26%). Never active at GO. Magnitude rises across consecutive trials toward the episode end, and the strongest activations are at D2 S1-rare on the final trials. Predicate: value < 4 and action a2, and either D1 with reward input 1 or D2 reaching S1. At D1 the action is the agent upcoming choice (marked FUTURE but it is the agent own computation, which is allowed); no future random outcome is used. A version using only the previous action at D1 scored worse (F1 0.58). Dev F1 0.81, mass recall 0.94. Not active on a1 trials, at GO, or before trial ~85.

issues: Several claims hold up. The unit is never active at GO (0 of 380k steps on dev and 0 of 396k on test). It is never active before ep_trial 80 (0 on both splits); 99.7% of the mass is at trials 90-99, and 100% is at value < 5.22. 99.5% of the mass is on action==2 trials. The phase split is 74% D1 / 26% D2. The original predicate reproduces: test P 0.746, R 0.777, F1 0.761, mass recall 0.908.

Systematic false-positive class: the D1 clause 'rewarded D1' is too broad. Among a2 trials with value<4, rewarded D1 steps fire only when the previous trial reached S2. With prev_state==2: dev P 0.960, test P 0.956. With prev_state==1: dev P 0.213 on 845 predicted steps, test P 0.192 on 1241. So the unit encodes 'reward just received from S2' (mostly common a2 rewarded), not reward in general. The label overclaims here.

The explanation states the observed-only predicate wrongly. The natural observed-only version, (value<4) & ((D1 & in_rew==1 & prev_action==2) | (D2 & in_state==1 & in_action==2)), scores dev F1 0.740 and test F1 0.693, not 0.58. The future 'action' variable therefore adds less than claimed. The gap is real (0.76 vs 0.69 on test) but modest.

The D2 clause is weak on its own: (value<4) & action==2 & D2 & state==1 has dev precision only 0.638 and holds 25% of the mass. Precision is higher when the previous trial also reached S1 (0.845) than when it reached S2 (0.591). This points to a build-up or accumulation effect rather than a clean 'rare S1 after a2' trigger.

Missed activations at D1 after reward 0 (persistence across steps within an active streak) hold about 5-7% of the mass: (value<4) & a2 & D1 & in_rew==0 has test mass 0.073 at P 0.27. These look like carry-over, not a separate condition.

Nearly all of the selectivity comes from value < 4 (the model's own value output), which works as a proxy for the episode ending. On their own, ep_trial thresholds do worse: ep>=92 gives dev F1 0.747 and ep>=94 gives 0.738. So 'end-of-episode' is really 'low predicted value'. The label already says this.
Test F1 is below the 0.8 bar. The refined predicate that excludes D1 steps after S1 raises it, but only to 0.786.
